article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Parsons is set to make his season debut tonight, the morning board still hasn't flipped to Week 12, and there are no cards yet — Check is how you get a verdict on your book's number.

items.headline: Parsons is set to debut tonight against the Rams
paragraphs: Green Bay activated Micah Parsons from the physically unable to perform list on Tuesday. He is medically cleared after ACL surgery and expected to make his season debut Wednesday night at the Rams, 8:00 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium.
He is officially questionable and likely on a snap count after 11 months out, so expect a limited role, not a full night. Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Parsons is activated, cleared, and expected to play tonight, officially questionable and likely on a snap count.

items.headline: Final injury picture for tonight: Jacobs unlikely, Rams' line thin
paragraphs: Josh Jacobs is questionable with a fractured finger and still not expected to play. He had surgery less than two weeks ago, and Kaleb Johnson would lead the backfield if he sits.

The Rams ruled out two starting offensive linemen, Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton, plus tight end Terrance Ferguson. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams stay on injured reserve. On the better side for Green Bay, linebacker Zaire Franklin is expected back after missing four games.

For Thursday: Kenneth Walker III practiced Tuesday and is trending back for Kansas City, Jake Ferguson is doubtful for Dallas, and Joe Milton III starts again for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out for the season.
items.takeaway: Jacobs is questionable but still not expected to play tonight. The Rams are down two starting linemen. Walker is trending back for Thursday; Ferguson is doubtful; Milton starts again Thursday for Philadelphia.

items.headline: Rain and wind still on for Thursday night in Buffalo
paragraphs: Kansas City at Buffalo, Thursday night, 8:20 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium: rain likely through the day and night, near 39 degrees, wind around 18 mph from the east-northeast.
The other three games this week are indoors: Rams-Packers at SoFi Stadium, Bears-Lions at Ford Field, and Eagles-Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Buffalo: rain likely all day and night, near 39 degrees, wind around 18 mph from the east-northeast. The Rams-Packers, Bears-Lions and Eagles-Cowboys games are all indoors.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The morning board still hasn't flipped to Week 12 — no cards yet
paragraphs: The board still shows Week 11 this morning, with all three headline cards — Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value — showing no play. That means no Week 12 cards to read yet, and no model numbers for tonight's game in the app.

Check the evening board for the first Week 12 lines. Meanwhile, the way to get a verdict on your book's number is Check: type in your book's line and price and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator.
items.takeaway: No Week 12 cards this morning because the board still shows Week 11 with empty headline cards. Check the evening board, and use Check on your own book's numbers in the meantime.

items.headline: The board doesn't know about Parsons yet — your book might
paragraphs: The app's numbers were built before Tuesday's news, so they don't reflect Parsons' return. Your book's line already has: the Rams have moved from -3.5 to -2.5 toward Green Bay.
That gap is exactly what Check is for. Put your book's price in and let the app re-evaluate it instead of guessing whether the move went too far.
items.takeaway: The app has not picked up today's news yet, so a line at your book may already reflect it. Run your book's number through Check rather than waiting for the board to catch up.

items.headline: Juice: the price of placing the bet
paragraphs: Juice — also called vig — is the small fee baked into the odds. When you see -110, that number is the juice: you risk $1.10 to win $1. The book keeps the extra 10 cents on the losing side, which is how it makes money win or lose.

Hypothetical example: you bet on two teams at -110 and split them, one win and one loss. You staked $1.10 on each, so you put $2.20 down and got $2.10 back — a 10-cent loss even though you went 1-1. That is the juice doing its job.
items.takeaway: A 1-1 day at -110 still loses money, so the price you pay matters as much as the team you pick.

items.headline: No Week 12 lines in the app yet — but the wider market has moved on Packers-Rams
paragraphs: The app still shows Week 11, so there is no app-tracked Week 12 movement to report. The wider market has moved on tonight's game: one tracker reports the Rams opened -3.5 and now sit at -2.5, a move toward Green Bay that lines up with Parsons' return being priced in.
DraftKings now lists the Rams at -2.5. That is reported movement, not an app verdict — the app has no Week 12 numbers yet, so run your book's price through Check before you decide what it's worth.
items.takeaway: No app-tracked Week 12 movement yet, but one tracker reports Rams-Packers moved from -3.5 to -2.5 toward Green Bay, and DraftKings now lists -2.5. That is reported movement, not an app verdict — run your book's number through Check.

items.headline: Tonight's game is a Check game, not a board game
paragraphs: There is no card on the board for Rams-Packers, so don't go looking for one. If your book has a number you like, type it into Check and let the app run it back through the model and evaluator. That is the verdict for tonight.
Inactives land about 90 minutes before the 8:00 p.m. ET kickoff, so the final word on Jacobs and Parsons comes around 6:30 p.m. ET. Wait for that before you lock anything in.
items.takeaway: No card on the board tonight, so use Check on your book's number — and wait for inactives about 90 minutes before the 8:00 p.m. ET kickoff before you lock anything in.

evidence.fact: Green Bay activated edge rusher Micah Parsons from the physically unable to perform list to the 53-man roster on Tuesday Nov 24, 2026, setting up his season debut Wednesday Nov 25 against the Rams. He is medically cleared after ACL surgery, officially questionable on the final injury report, and expected to play on a limited snap count after 11 months out.
evidence.interpretation: Parsons' return strengthens Green Bay's pass rush, but a snap count after 11 months out limits how much of the game he can affect.

evidence.fact: Final Week 12 injury reports, Tuesday Nov 24, 2026: Josh Jacobs (Packers, finger) questionable on the final report, limited in all three practices, still not expected to play Wednesday after finger surgery less than two weeks ago; Kaleb Johnson would lead the backfield if he sits. Rams ruled out G Steve Avila (hamstring), C Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and TE Terrance Ferguson; Puka Nacua and Davante Adams remain on injured reserve. Packers LB Zaire Franklin is expected back after missing four games. Kenneth Walker III (Chiefs, groin) practiced Tuesday and is trending back for Thursday. Jake Ferguson (Cowboys) is doubtful for Thursday. Joe Milton III starts again Thursday for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out for the season.
evidence.interpretation: Green Bay is likely without its lead back but gets its star pass rusher back; the Rams are thin on the offensive line and at receiver.
